findings.issue: Stale compatibility claim now contradicted by the change. The line reads "The Backstage core libraries and plugins are compatible with all versions of React from v17 to v18", but this run narrowed every published peer range to react/react-dom/@types/react ^18.0.0, so React 17 is no longer accepted by any core library or plugin. The info banner at line 9 also only mentions removing React 16 support. CLAUDE.md requires behavior changes to carry documentation updates and the change plan has no docs unit covering this file.
findings.fix: Update line 13 to state that the core libraries and plugins require React 18 (React 17 is no longer supported), and extend the line 9 info banner to mention React 17 removal alongside React 16. Leave the step-by-step narrative at lines 125 and 129 alone (it describes the in-progress migration state), and do not touch docs/releases/*.

The "Unlisted dependencies" table still has the row `| react-dom | src/lib/bundler/hasReactDomClient.ts:21:22 | error |` pointing at a file deleted by this run, and the heading still says "Unlisted dependencies (2)" (line 12). findings.fix: Remove the react-dom row and change the heading count from (2) to (1), leaving the `react | src/lib/bundler/server.ts:274:43` row intact (U15 was a one-line replacement so that line number is unchanged). Equivalent to re-running `yarn build:knip-reports` for this package.

findings.issue: Closing line is `**Affected components:** none`. .changeset/README.md mandates that a @backstage/ui changeset end with `**Affected components:**` plus comma-separated component names, and there is no precedent for `none` anywhere in packages/ui/CHANGELOG.md. useBreakpoint is a public export of @backstage/ui and is consumed internally by useBg and useDefinition, so the entry is also understating reach. Everything else about the file is correct: no markdown headings, no **Migration:** section (not a breaking change), and patch is the right level for 0.19.0 below 1.0.0.
findings.fix: Replace `none` with the affected surface, e.g. `**Affected components:** useBreakpoint` (or name the components that consume it), so the file satisfies the mandated format.
